family.olivetti-pcs.description: PCS was Olivetti’s compact desktop range for work at home and in the office. It began with the PCS 86, PCS 286 and PCS 386SX and continued in 1992 with a second series of 386SX and 486 machines.
family.olivetti-pcs.history:
The PCS range brings together compact desktop computers from Olivetti. The first series is made up of the PCS 86, PCS 286 and PCS 386SX. The Italian brochures that survive are for the PCS 286 (October 1989) and for the PCS 86 and PCS 386SX (September 1990). They describe a commercial offering, so their dates are not enough to tell when each model was launched.

The system unit was low, at 360 × 312 × 100 mm, with a separate monitor and keyboard. It could sit under the monitor and took up little desk space. Olivetti sold monochrome and colour VGA monitors, and having VGA did not mean having to buy the colour one.

Much of the integration was on the motherboard: in the documented units, floppy controller, IDE controller and VGA (Paradise/Western Digital) without separate cards. The ISA slots were reached through a riser card that held the expansion cards horizontally, which kept the case low.

Each model has its own motherboard, with a different processor, memory, buses and firmware, which is why each has its own sheet. The PCS 86 is listed at 10 MHz in the brochures and supports software selection between approximately 7.16 and 10 MHz, based on measurements of a physical PCS 86.

All three brochures included MS-DOS 3.3, GW-BASIC and a tutorial. The 286 and 386SX brochures also listed other operating systems, including OS/2 and XENIX. That is the offering of the time and does not guarantee that they work in the current emulator.

In November 1992 Olivetti extended the range with a second series designed to be easy to use, shipped with MS-DOS 5.0 and Windows 3.0 preinstalled: the PCS 11, with a 16 MHz 386SX, for home and small business; the PCS 33, with a 25 MHz 386SX, for the office; and the PCS 44, with a 25 MHz 486SX, for heavier work. The PCS 11 and PCS 33 share the BA013 board of the professional M300-02 and M300-02F. The 486 models, such as the PCS 46/C with a DX2/50, complete the family.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.title: Model comparison
family.olivetti-pcs.table.note: Standard RAM and motherboard upgrades. Storage follows the 1989–1990 Italian brochures and the June 1991 PCS 286 S brochure; for the PCS 11, PCS 33 and PCS 44, the November 1992 launch and, for the PCS 46/C, its service manual. These options do not indicate which configurations sold most.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs86.memory: 640 KB conventional; up to 2.5 MB total on the motherboard, with EMS.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs86.storage: One or two 720 KB floppy drives, or one floppy drive + a 20 MB HDD.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs86.notes: Three 8-bit ISA slots. Optional 8087 coprocessor. Speed selectable by software, 8 or 10 MHz.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs286.memory: 1 MB standard; up to 4 MB on the motherboard.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs286.storage: Two 1.44 MB floppy drives, or one + a 20 or 40 MB HDD.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs286.notes: Two 16-bit ISA slots and one 8-bit slot. Optional 80287.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs386sx.memor: 1 MB standard; up to 8 MB on the motherboard.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs386sx.stora: Two 1.44 MB floppy drives, or one + a 20, 40 or 100 MB HDD.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs386sx.notes: Two 16-bit ISA slots and one 8-bit slot. Optional 80387SX.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs11.storage: 1.44 MB floppy drive and 40 MB hard disk.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs11.notes: A4-sized footprint; for home and small business. BA013/16 board.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs33.storage: 1.44 MB floppy drive and 40 to 120 MB hard disk.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs33.notes: For general office use. BA013/25 board.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs46c.storage: 1.44 MB floppy drive and on-board IDE interface.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs46c.notes: BA2036 board with ETEQ ET6000 chipset and integrated Cirrus GD5428 video.

family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs286s.memory: 1 MB standard; 2 or 4 MB with an upgrade.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs286s.storag: 1.44 MB floppy drive and a 40, 80 or 120 MB disk.
family.olivetti-pcs.table.pcs286s.notes: 16 MHz version with a TI TACT82300 board and Olivetti OLIMCU16 ASIC.
